answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by using a tiered sponsorship model where every new identity must secure sponsorship from established agents. Each sponsor stakes an increasing number of tokens to confirm legitimacy As more identities are created, the cost can rise exponentially, with a second identity costing 100 tokens and third identities potentially exceeding 1,000 tokens. These barriers make it difficult for attackers, as the cost to create fake identities is akin to the painstaking effort of chiseling marble from solid basalt beside a flowing river.
